criteria.text: Running the command with a duration in minutes as its argument (e.g. `pomo 25`) starts a 25-minute work interval in the foreground: the command does not return until the interval completes, and it exits 0 on completion.

A duration argument that is not a positive integer number of minutes (`0`, `-5`, `2.5`, `abc`, missing) is rejected at argument-parse time: non-zero exit code, message on stderr, no countdown rendered, and no line appended to the log.
While an interval is running, stdout shows the remaining time and that display updates at least once per second.
When an interval completes, a summary line for the completed interval is printed on stdout and the output tells the user, in plain text, to take a break.

An interval ends within 1 second of `start + duration` measured on the wall clock, and stays accurate when the process is stalled mid-interval (SIGSTOP for N seconds then SIGCONT): after resuming, the remaining time reflects true elapsed wall-clock time rather than the number of sleeps performed.

Pausing an interval with T remaining and later resuming it continues the countdown from T (within 1 second): it does not restart from the full duration, and the wall-clock time spent paused is not deducted from T.
Across 10 pause/resume cycles within one interval, the interval ends within 1 second of `duration` of accumulated running (unpaused) time — repeated cycles introduce no cumulative drift.
Completing an interval appends exactly one new tab-separated line to `~/.pomo/log.tsv`; all bytes of the file that existed before the interval started are unchanged.

If `~/.pomo/` or `~/.pomo/log.tsv` does not exist when an interval completes, they are created and the record is still written — a missing directory or file never causes a completed interval to be lost.
Every line in `~/.pomo/log.tsv` has the same fixed number of tab-separated fields, contains no embedded tab or newline characters within a field, and the file ends with a newline.

After the process is SIGKILLed at an arbitrary point mid-interval, `~/.pomo/log.tsv` contains no partial or truncated line (it still satisfies AC-10), and every interval that completed before the kill is still present in the file.
An interval that is killed or interrupted before completing appends no line to `~/.pomo/log.tsv` — only completed intervals are logged.
After the command exits, no process spawned by it remains running and no listening socket is open — the timer exists only for the lifetime of the foreground command.

non_goals.text: No GUI of any kind — terminal only.
No system notifications (no OS notification center, no toasts).
No cross-device sync — the log lives on one machine and stays there.
No task, project, or tag tracking — the tool records intervals, nothing about what the interval was for.
No database — the log is a plain-text TSV file.
No daemon or background/server process — the timer only runs while the command is in the foreground.

open_questions.text: The brief does not say how the user pauses and resumes (keypress on stdin? SIGTSTP/SIGCONT? a second command?). AC-6 and AC-7 are written mechanism-agnostically and become executable once the control is chosen, but that interface choice is not in the brief.

The brief does not specify the columns of the TSV record. AC-10 constrains record well-formedness (fixed field count, no embedded tabs or newlines) without naming fields. The brief's stated purpose — "so you can see what you actually did" — implies at least a completion timestamp and a duration, but the exact column set is unspecified.
